instructions: Put the raisins in a small bowl of warm water and leave them for 5 minutes. Mince the garlic.
Toast the pine nuts in a large dry pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until they're golden and smell toasty. Transfer them to a bowl.
Drain the raisins and shake off the extra water.
Add the olive oil and garlic to the same pan over medium heat. Cook for 20 to 30 seconds, until you can smell the garlic.
Add the spinach a big handful at a time, stirring each one until it wilts before adding the next. When all of it is in, cook for 2 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the pine nuts, raisins, salt and pepper.
Transfer to a serving dish. Serve warm or at room temperature.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Spain on a Fork and Wine & Spirits agree on spinach wilted in olive oil with garlic, raisins and pine nuts; Wine & Spirits adds garbanzo beans and a splash of sherry vinegar, which others call a different Andalusian dish, so they are left out. This follows Spain on a Fork, soaking the raisins first. It is really a side dish, so it is best planned alongside something else. Spain on a Fork has one rating, so this is a fallback lead.
